newsitem.title: RUSSIA: G7, Russian energy ministers to meet in Moscow.
newsitem.headline: G7, Russian energy ministers to meet in Moscow.

text.p: Moscow will host a meeting of energy ministers from the Group of Seven (G7) rich industrial nations plus Russia next year, the Russian and U.S. energy ministers said after talks on Monday.

"We discussed issues on the future energy summit which will be in Moscow, probably in March or April of 1998 before the summit of the eight," Russian First Deputy Prime Minister and Energy Minister Boris Nemtsov told reporters.
Heads of state and government from the G7 and Russian President Boris Yeltsin are due to meet at a summit of eight in Birmingham, England on May 15-17 next year.

"I look forward to coming back early next year when the energy summit, which was recommended by President Yeltsin, will be held here in Moscow," U.S. Secretary of Energy Federico Pena said after meeting Nemtsov.
"It will be the first energy summit of the ministers of the Eight," he added.

Nemtsov said the ministerial meeting would look at global energy issues as well as at investment in the Russian energy sector -- one of the key areas in which the reform-minded Moscow government sees significant growth and prosperity.
The G7 countries are the United States, Britain, France, Germany, Japan, Italy and Canada.
U.S. embassy and Russian officials denied a report by Itar-Tass news agency that President Bill Clinton would attend an energy summit hosted by Yeltsin in Moscow were wrong.
"The president has no such plans," U.S. embassy spokesman Richard Hoagland said.
"The (Tass) interpretation is incorrect," Nemtsov's spokesman Andrei Pershin told Reuters. "Nemtsov meant a meeting of energy ministers, which will take place in March or April."
